transfer.recovery: 1) Unlock the spindle, index back to the zero hole (the S8 position) and lock it. 2) With the DTI in the spindle, run the tip down the reamed Ø11.43 crank-bore wall by quill feed, once on the -Y side and once on the +Y side. 3) Each reading holds within one dial division (0.0005 in) over the bore depth: the post has not turned, the head has moved. Re-align the head as in S4 (tap the head body on the table, never the work, until the top and side sweeps of the body along X each read within 0.01 mm, then tighten the head bolts), re-index to the plate setting and sweep again. The zeros stand. 4) A reading moves more than one division: the post has turned in the jaws. hold.clamp: AUTHOR'S CHOICE: clamp the post with the cap bridge (C1) while the saw vise is still open; the cradle is moved and gripped only in op 10.

clamps.note: brass pad on the south cap annulus, which S2 op 40 leaves 0.045 proud; tighten both nuts evenly. The load runs down the cone sleeve onto the cradle's north-cap land, not through the bonded joint; studs at Y+-30 clear the body

hold.locate: first scribe a line round the post 87.75 mm from foot B for the blade centre (foot B down on the surface plate, height gauge). Lay the post in both cradle seats with the crank sleeve up and turn it until the north cap annulus sits flat on the north-cap land; the cap faces square the cone cross-bore to the saw bed
hold.note: Cradle and bridge: made once before first use to the two SHOP-MADE FIXTURE tables and their Make: lines (sheet 2). Contact check before the first cut: wipe layout blue on the north-cap land and the brass pad, seat the post and tighten the bridge, then take the bridge off and lift the post out. Each must print on its cap annulus and leave no blue on the body. Tighten the bridge nuts wrench-tight: the saw's feed thrust tries to lift the foot end.
hold.stop: AUTHOR'S CHOICE: no end stop along the post: the north cap on its land and the bridge on the south cap fix it in the cradle, and op 10 sets the blade to the scribed line.

hold.clamp: AUTHOR'S CHOICE: seat a button in each end of the journal bore, close the soft jaws on the two buttons with the crank sleeve over the front jaw, tap B down on the parallels and tighten. Contact check before cutting: look along each jaw: daylight must show between the jaw and the body all round both buttons. The cap faces square the cross-bore to the jaws, so no clocking is needed; the jaw tops stay 8.6 mm under the head shoulder and 10.9 mm under the crank sleeve.

findings.message: S4: holding and cutting decisions are declared; this does not approve measured fixture clearance.

hold.clamp: AUTHOR'S CHOICE: tighten each independent jaw a little at a time while indicating. Then align the head with the table: with the DTI in the spindle, sweep the top of the body along X from foot B to the shoulder, then its side; tap the head on the table until each sweep reads within 0.01 mm, tighten the head bolts and re-check both sweeps and the runout. Remove the key and lock the spindle before drilling.
hold.grip_on: AUTHOR'S CHOICE: the last 20 mm of the raw tail; the tail end seats on the chuck body face
hold.note: AUTHOR'S CHOICE: reamer trial bores, made once before the dividing head goes on the table, because a solid reamer has no size adjustment and the part is only reamed after the sleeves are bonded: the 0.4500 in reamer (11.430) sits 0.013 under the top of the 11.413-11.443 crank band, and the 0.4835 in reamer (12.281) only 0.004 under the top of the 12.256-12.285 journal band. Saw two 1018 offcuts about 15 mm long, one from the 25 mm crank bar and one from the 3/4 in cone bar, and grip each in the mill vise on parallels with the bore line clear of them. Crank offcut: spot it with the #2 centre drill, drill 11.2 through at the S8 op 20 speed and feed, then ream it with the 0.4500 in reamer at the S8 op 30 speed and feed. Journal offcut: spot it, drill 12.05 through at the S9 op 20 speed and feed, then ream it with the 0.4835 in reamer at the S9 op 30 speed and feed. Use cutting oil and a steady quill feed; run each drill point and the reamer lead fully out of the far side. Bore-gauge each trial bore at both mouths: the crank trial must read 11.413-11.443 and the journal trial 12.256-12.285. If either reads over, that reamer cuts oversize: do not take it to the part; replace it and ream a new trial.
hold.stop: AUTHOR'S CHOICE: caliper the post from foot B to the raw tail end first: it must read 125.0, as S1 op 10 left it. Tail end against the chuck body face, so 105 mm of post stands out of the jaws. Indicate the turned head and body to run true within 0.02 mm, then indicate foot B square to the head axis.

inspection_method: AUTHOR'S CHOICE: qualify each gauge rod before use. Micrometer it at both ends and the middle: the three readings must agree within 0.0001 in (one division) and match its size. Then lay it in the V-blocks on the surface plate, DTI tip on top over each block and at the middle, and turn it one full turn: each reading must stay within one dial division (0.0005 in). A rod that fails either check is not used.

AUTHOR'S CHOICE: slide the Ø11.405 gauge rod through the crank bore and the Ø12.250 gauge rod through the journal bore, each with about 40 mm out of both ends. By the op 100 and op 110 bore readings each rod is 0.006-0.038 mm under its bore. Seat each rod by gravity on the low line of its bore, pressing it down by hand at both mouths: lying along that line over the full bore length, the rod stays parallel to the bore axis, so the clearance moves both readings of a rise equally and cancels.

Mount the DTI on the height gauge, tip on top of the rod with the lever lifted to mid-travel (about 0.015 in of its 0.030 in); a higher rod reads +. At each position sweep the tip across the rod and take the highest reading. Write every reading in mm: inch dial × 25.4.

Seating check, at every position: read, press the rod down with a finger at the far mouth, read again; the two must agree within one dial division (0.0005 in). If not, the rod rocks on a bellmouthed mouth: wipe rod and bore, reseat and repeat. Then roll the rod half a turn in its bore and repeat the rise; record the mean of the two rises, so a bend in the rod cancels.

Lay a parallel on the plate in line with the rod and stand the second 1-2-3 block at its end as the stop. Position A: height-gauge base against the stop. Position B: the first 1-2-3 block between stop and base, 2 in face (50.8) for the journal rod, 3 in face (76.2) for the crank rod. Rise = reading at B − reading at A.

Place the stop so position A puts the tip about 4 mm outside the north cap on the journal rod, or about 2 mm outside the flush crank-sleeve end on the crank rod; position B then lands just outside the south cap, or just outside the projecting crank-sleeve end.
Orientation 1, foot B on the plate. Journal rod rise: {rJ1}
Orientation 1, foot B on the plate. Crank rod rise: {rC1}

Orientation 2: lay the post on the plate on its head and body, chocked with a 1 in parallel each side, and wrap tape round the crank rod at its lower mouth so it cannot slide. Roll the post until the journal rod rise reads within ±0.05 with the projecting crank-sleeve end rising. Journal rod rise: {rJ2}
Orientation 2, crank rod: set the DTI to zero at A, move to B and raise the height gauge until the DTI reads zero again. Height-gauge rise (ideal 76.2 × tan 12.5182° = 16.918): {rC2}

transfer.recovery: 1) Unlock the spindle, index back to the zero hole (the S4 position) and lock it. 2) With the DTI in the spindle, run the tip down the reamed Ø22.01 crank-socket wall by quill feed, once on the -Y side and once on the +Y side. 3) Each reading holds within one dial division (0.0005 in) over the socket depth: the post has not turned, the head has moved. Re-align the head as in S4 (tap the head body on the table, never the work, until the top and side sweeps of the body along X each read within 0.01 mm, then tighten the head bolts), re-index to the plate setting and sweep again. The zeros stand. 4) A reading moves more than one division: the post has turned in the jaws. This is the only case that moves the work: ease one jaw, turn the post until both socket-wall readings hold one division, re-tighten each jaw a little at a time while indicating the head and body to 0.02 mm, re-index, then set the Y, X and Z zeros again from the start of this table.
